evidence_slice: Historic England's official 'Understanding List Entries' guidance, updated 21 January 2025, explains the NHLE map convention: a small blue triangle generally denotes buildings listed before April 2011 and may not be positioned in the centre of the building or buildings, whereas buildings added to the List after April 2011 are denoted by a blue polygon. It also explains that older records were migrated as legacy data. Applied to the already-verified Rougemont Castle List Entry 1104054, first listed 29 January 1953, this source is an exact policy-level blocker rather than footprint evidence: the guidance does not supply record-level polygon coordinates for this legacy entry.

field_evidence.footprint: Official guidance states pre-April-2011 listed buildings are generally denoted by a small blue triangle, which may not be positioned in the centre of the building or buildings; this is not record-level footprint polygon geometry.
field_evidence.type_use: Rougemont Castle identity/type remains established by already-verified lineage evidence; this new policy window is used only to resolve the missing-footprint criterion.
field_evidence.coverage: Official guidance contrasts pre-April-2011 triangle representation with blue polygons for buildings added after April 2011.
